definition_zh: 部门；行业；扇形；区域
definition_en: a distinct part of an economy or society, a particular area of business, a slice-shaped part of a circle, or a separate district
core_image: 一张饼图被切成几块，每块颜色不同，旁边标着各自的比例
scene: 报告用一张饼图拆开了国民经济的几大部门。The service sector now employs most workers.
sceneCN: 这里 sector 是「部门」（第 1 个义项）；句意：服务业部门如今雇用了大多数劳动者。

senses.title: Part of an economy
senses.definition: a distinct part of a country's economy or society
senses.definitionCN: 一国经济或社会中相对独立的一部分
senses.example: The service sector is growing fast.
senses.exampleCN: 服务业部门增长很快。
senses.why: Economists divide national activity into sectors.
senses.whyCN: 经济学家把国民活动划分成若干部门。

senses.title: Area of business
senses.definition: a particular area of business activity
senses.definitionCN: 某一特定的商业活动领域
senses.example: She works in the technology sector.
senses.exampleCN: 她在科技行业工作。
senses.why: The word labels industries such as banking or farming.
senses.whyCN: 该词用来标记银行、农业等行业。

senses.title: Slice of a circle
senses.definition: a plane figure bounded by two radii and an arc
senses.definitionCN: 由两条半径和一段弧围成的平面图形
senses.example: Draw a sector of the circle in the diagram.
senses.exampleCN: 在图上画一个圆的扇形。
senses.why: The geometric sense keeps the idea of a cut-out part.
senses.whyCN: 几何义保留了「切分出来的一块」这个意象。

senses.title: Separate district
senses.definition: a distinct part of an area, especially in military use
senses.definitionCN: 某一区域中相对独立的部分，尤用于军事
senses.example: Troops held the northern sector of the city.
senses.exampleCN: 部队控制了城市的北部区域。
senses.why: A sector can also be a piece of physical ground.
senses.whyCN: sector 也可以指地面上划分出的一块。

intro.en: Sector comes from Latin sector, a cutter, from secare, to cut.
intro.cn: sector 源自拉丁语 sector（切割者），出自 secare（切）。

items.en: Secare meant to cut or divide.
items.cn: secare 意为切、分割。

items.en: Sector named a cutter and later a division.
items.cn: sector 起初指切割者，后来指划分出的部分。

items.en: The word entered English for a geometric slice.
items.cn: 该词以几何扇形的意义进入英语。

items.en: It extended to parts of an economy.
items.cn: 它又扩展到经济部门的含义。

items.en: Today it labels industries and city districts.
items.cn: 如今它用来标记各行业与城区。

note.en: Sector is compared with similar-looking words and with words for parts or divisions.
note.cn: 把 sector 与形近词以及表示部分、划分的词作比较。

definition_zh: 安全的；牢固的；获得；使安全
definition_en: safe from danger, firmly fixed, to succeed in getting something, or to make something safe
core_image: 门上新换的锁舌咔哒一声扣进锁扣，链条也挂好了
scene: 他换了新锁，又把窗户逐一检查了一遍。She secured the door before leaving.
sceneCN: 这里 secure 是「使安全」（第 4 个义项）；句意：她离开前把门锁好。

senses.title: Safe from danger
senses.definition: protected from harm or risk
senses.definitionCN: 受到保护而免于伤害或风险
senses.example: Keep your passport in a secure place.
senses.exampleCN: 把护照放在安全的地方。
senses.why: This is the basic sense of being free from danger.
senses.whyCN: 这是「免于危险」的基本义。

senses.title: Firmly fixed
senses.definition: fixed so firmly that it cannot move or be opened
senses.definitionCN: 固定得很牢，不会移动或被打开
senses.example: Make sure the ladder is secure.
senses.exampleCN: 确保梯子固定牢靠。
senses.why: Something firmly fastened is also safe.
senses.whyCN: 固定牢靠的东西同样是安全的。

senses.title: Obtain
senses.definition: to succeed in getting something
senses.definitionCN: 成功地得到某物
senses.example: She secured a place at university.
senses.exampleCN: 她获得了大学的录取名额。
senses.why: Getting something safely is the verb sense.
senses.whyCN: 稳妥地得到某物，是它的动词义。

senses.title: Make safe
senses.definition: to protect something from danger or loss
senses.definitionCN: 保护某物免受危险或损失
senses.example: Guards secured the building.
senses.exampleCN: 警卫守住了大楼。
senses.why: The verb can mean to fasten or guard a place.
senses.whyCN: 动词也可表示把某处锁好或守住。

intro.cn: secure 源自拉丁语 securus（无忧的），由 se-（无）与 cura（忧虑）构成。

items.en: Cura meant care or worry.
items.cn: cura 意为关心、忧虑。

items.cn: securus 形容一个人无忧无虑。

items.cn: securitas 指安全与免于恐惧。

items.en: English secure first meant free from fear.
items.cn: 英语 secure 最初意为免于恐惧。

items.en: The word later meant to fasten and to obtain.
items.cn: 后来该词又表示固定牢靠与获得。

note.en: Secure is compared with similar-looking words and with words for safety.
note.cn: 把 secure 与形近词以及表示安全的词作比较。

examples.en: She secured a place at university.

definition_zh: 安全；保障；保安；证券
definition_en: the state of being safe, protection against danger, the guards who protect a place, or financial assets such as shares

scene: 进大楼前，每个人都要把包放上检查台。Airport security checked every bag.

senses.title: Protection

senses.whyCN: 具体措施把「安全」变成了可计数的概念。

definition_zh: 沉积物；沉淀物；泥沙；沉淀（动词）
definition_en: solid material that settles at the bottom of a liquid, or that is carried and laid down by water, wind or ice
core_image: 浑浊的河水在入海口慢下来，细沙一粒粒沉到瓶底，清水留在上层
scene: 河水灌进玻璃瓶，静置到第二天早晨，细泥沉到瓶底，上层的液体变清了。Fine sediment settled to the bottom of the jar by morning.
sceneCN: 这里 sediment 指「液体中沉降到底部的固体颗粒」（第 1 个义项：沉积下来的泥沙等固体物质）；句意为细小的沉积物在夜里沉到瓶底。可辨识物件：玻璃瓶、浑浊河水、瓶底细泥、上层清水。

senses.title: Material laid down by water, wind or ice
senses.titleCN: 由水、风或冰堆积下来的物质
senses.definition: solid particles carried by water, wind or ice and left behind when the carrier loses energy
senses.definitionCN: 指被水、风或冰搬运、在搬运介质失去能量后留下的固体颗粒
senses.example: Fine sediment settled to the bottom of the jar by morning.
senses.exampleCN: 细小的沉积物在夜里沉到了瓶底。
senses.why: Sedere 'to sit' plus -mentum 'result' gives 'what has sat down'; the word names the material only after it has stopped moving.
senses.whyCN: sedere「坐」加 -mentum「结果」给出「已经坐下来的东西」；这个词只在那物质停止移动之后才命名它。

senses.title: Solids that settle in a liquid
senses.titleCN: 液体中沉到底部的固体
senses.definition: the solid matter that sinks to the bottom of a standing liquid
senses.definitionCN: 指在静置液体中下沉到底部的固体物质
senses.example: A dark sediment gathered at the bottom of the kettle.
senses.exampleCN: 水壶底部积起一层深色沉淀。
senses.why: It is the same settling seen in a kitchen: any liquid left standing leaves its solids behind.
senses.whyCN: 这是厨房里也能见到的同一种沉降：任何静置的液体都会把固体留在底部。

senses.title: A deposited layer or stratum
senses.titleCN: 沉积形成的一层或一层岩层
senses.definition: a single bed or layer of deposited material, often visible as a band
senses.definitionCN: 指沉积形成的一层材料，常呈带状可见
senses.example: Each sediment band records a different flood.
senses.exampleCN: 每一层沉积都记录了一次不同的洪水。
senses.why: Once the deposit is thick enough to see, it becomes a layer, and the noun moves from material to a visible band.
senses.whyCN: 一旦沉积厚到肉眼可见，它就成了一层，名词也从材料转向可见的层带。

senses.title: Suspended load in moving water
senses.definition: particles held in suspension in a river or current, measured as water quality
senses.definitionCN: 指河流或水流中悬而未落的颗粒，作为水质指标测定
senses.example: The dam traps sediment that once reached the delta.
senses.exampleCN: 大坝拦住了原本到达三角洲的悬移质。
senses.why: Particles that have not yet settled are still sediment, so the word follows the material through its whole journey.
senses.whyCN: 尚未落下的颗粒仍然是 sediment，因此这个词跟着物质走完整个搬运过程。

senses.title: Lees at the bottom of wine or vinegar
senses.definition: the deposit of dead yeast and particles found in wine, cider or vinegar
senses.definitionCN: 指葡萄酒、苹果酒或醋中死酵母与颗粒形成的沉渣
senses.example: Pour the wine slowly so the sediment stays in the bottle.
senses.exampleCN: 慢慢倒酒，让沉渣留在瓶里。
senses.why: Wine lees are the household version of the geological process, so the same noun serves both.
senses.whyCN: 酒渣是这一地质过程在厨房里的版本，因此同一个名词两边都用。

senses.title: Accumulated remains of the past
senses.titleCN: 比喻：历史或记忆的层层积存
senses.definition: figurative: the accumulated, slowly deposited remains of an earlier period
senses.definitionCN: 比喻用法：较早时期缓慢积存下来的遗留物
senses.example: Old letters lay in the sediment of family memory.
senses.exampleCN: 旧信件沉在家族记忆的底层。
senses.why: The metaphor works because memory also deposits slowly and in layers, with older things lower down.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻成立，是因为记忆也缓慢、分层地沉积，越老的东西越靠下。

senses.title: To deposit as sediment (technical verb)
senses.definition: to cause particles to settle out of a liquid, or to deposit them
senses.definitionCN: 指使颗粒从液体中沉降出来，或把它们沉积下来
senses.example: The current sediments sand along the inner bend.
senses.exampleCN: 水流把砂沉积在内侧河弯。
senses.why: English verbs form freely from nouns, and technical writing needs a verb for the act of depositing.
senses.whyCN: 英语动词可由名词自由构成，而技术写作需要一个动词来表达「使沉积」这一动作。

senses.title: The geological archive of a basin
senses.definition: the whole body of deposits in a basin, read as a record of past environments
senses.definitionCN: 指盆地中全部沉积体，被当作过去环境的记录来解读
senses.example: The sediment of the lake bed spans ten thousand years.
senses.exampleCN: 湖底的沉积层跨越了一万年。
senses.why: A basin's whole fill is read as a record, so the mass noun becomes a collective archive.
senses.whyCN: 盆地的全部充填物被当作记录来读，于是这个物质名词变成了集体档案。

intro.en: Sediment comes from the Latin noun for a settling, built on the verb 'to sit'. The geological sense is a later specialization of a very general image.
intro.cn: sediment 来自拉丁语表示「沉降」的名词，由动词「坐、停留」构成；地质义是这个极普遍意象后来的专门化。

items.en: Sedere 'to sit, stay, settle' is a second-conjugation verb with the stem sed-, and it underlies a large family: session, resident, sedentary, sedative.
items.cn: sedere「坐、停留、安定」是第二变格法动词，词干 sed-，支撑起一个大家族：session、resident、sedentary、sedative。

items.en: Sedimentum 'a settling, a sinking down, dregs' was formed with -mentum, the suffix for the result of an action, so the noun names what has settled rather than the settling itself.
items.cn: sedimentum「沉降、沉下、渣滓」由 -mentum 构成，这个后缀表示动作的结果，因此名词命名的是「沉下来的东西」，而不是「下沉」这一动作。

items.en: English took the word through French sédiment in the sixteenth century, first for dregs and earthy matter in liquids.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪经法语 sédiment 借入这个词，最初指液体中的渣滓与土质物。

items.en: From the eighteenth century sediment was applied to sand, mud and gravel laid down by water, and the noun became central to stratigraphy.
items.cn: 从十八世纪起，sediment 被用于水所堆积的砂、泥与砾石，这个名词成为地层学的核心。

items.en: The verb sedimented appears later, chiefly in technical writing, where it means to settle out or to deposit particles.
items.cn: 动词 sedimented 出现较晚，主要用于技术写作，意为沉降析出或使颗粒沉积。

items.en: Not uncertain: the derivation from sedere is established. What is reconstructed is the Indo-European root *sed- 'sit', which is inferred from Sanskrit and Greek cognates rather than attested directly.
items.cn: 并非存疑：源自 sedere 这一点是确定的。属重构的是印欧词根 *sed-「坐」，它由梵语与希腊语同族词推断而来，而非直接实证。

note.en: Group one holds words that look like sediment but come from other roots; group two holds materials and processes often named beside it.
note.cn: 第一组是外形近似但词根不同的词；第二组是常与它并称的材料与过程词。

entries.definition: Means a feeling or opinion, from Latin sentire 'to feel'; the shared letters sed- are accidental, since the root here is sent-.
entries.definitionCN: 意为情感或看法，来自拉丁 sentire「感觉」；共同的字母只是巧合，这里的词根是 sent-。

entries.definition: A calming drug, from sedare 'to settle, calm', a causative form of sedere; it shares the root 'sit' but means 'making something settle down'.
entries.definitionCN: 指镇静药，来自 sedare「使安定」，是 sedere 的使动形式；它共享「坐」的词根，但意思是「使某物安定下来」。

entries.definition: Means sitting much or fixed in one place, from sedere plus -ary; it is a true relative and describes the posture, not the deposit.
entries.definitionCN: 意为久坐的、固定一处的，来自 sedere 加 -ary；它是真正的同族词，描写姿势而非沉积物。

entries.definition: A meeting or sitting of a body, from sedere through Latin sessio; related in root, unrelated in meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 指机构的一次会议或开庭，经拉丁 sessio 来自 sedere；词根相关，意义无关。

entries.definition: Any material left by a natural process, or the act of laying it down; it is the wider word that sediment belongs to.
entries.definitionCN: 指任何自然过程留下的物质或堆积动作；它是 sediment 所属的更宽泛的词。

entries.definition: Specifically sediment of grains between sand and clay in size; it is one size class of sediment, not a synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 特指粒径介于砂与黏土之间的细粒沉积物；它只是沉积物的一个粒级，不是同义词。

entries.definition: Thick wet waste from sewage or industry; it stresses pollution and disposal, while sediment is neutral.
entries.definitionCN: 指污水或工业产生的黏稠湿废物；它强调污染与处置，sediment 则是中性词。

entries.definition: Solid matter thrown out of a solution by a chemical reaction, not by simple settling; chemistry keeps the two apart.
entries.definitionCN: 指化学反应从溶液中析出的固体，而非单纯沉降；化学上二者区分明确。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin verb, the real suffix and the real geological phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁动词、真实的后缀与真实的地质搭配。

normal.en: Sedere 'to sit' plus -mentum 'result': the stuff that has sat down at the bottom.
normal.cn: sedere「坐」加 -mentum「结果」：已经坐到底部的东西。

normal.en: The family runs sediment, sedimentary, sedimentation, sedimentology.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 sediment、sedimentary、sedimentation、sedimentology。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: fine sediment, suspended sediment, sediment core, sediment transport.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：细沉积物、悬浮沉积物、沉积柱样、沉积物搬运。

normal.en: The same root gives session, resident and sedentary, all about sitting or staying.
normal.cn: 同一词根衍生 session、resident、sedentary，都与坐或停留有关。

normal.en: In a river the sediment travels high in flood and rests low in drought.
normal.cn: 在河里，沉积物洪水时高悬、枯水时落底。

abstract.en: Picture a clock that records time by dropping sand instead of moving hands.
abstract.cn: 想象一座靠落沙而非指针记录时间的钟。

abstract.en: Picture a library where every reader leaves one grain on the floor.
abstract.cn: 想象一座图书馆，每位读者都在地板上留下一粒沙。

abstract.en: Picture a river writing its diary in mud at the bottom of a lake.
abstract.cn: 想象一条河在湖底用泥写下自己的日记。

examples.en: The reservoir is filling with sediment faster than expected.
examples.cn: 水库正以超出预期的速度被泥沙填满。

examples.en: A core of lake sediment shows layers of ash from old eruptions.
examples.cn: 一根湖底沉积柱样显示出古老喷发留下的层层火山灰。

examples.en: Let the vinegar stand until the sediment sinks.
examples.cn: 让醋静置到沉渣落下。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「塞（se）底（di）闷（ment）」——塞在底下的东西 → 沉积物、沉淀

root: 拉丁 sedere「坐、停留」+ -mentum（动作结果）→ sedimentum「沉降、沉渣」；英语经法语 sédiment 借入。印欧词根 *sed-「坐」属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one motion: particles lose their energy and sit down, and that single settling then becomes a layer, a load, a wine lees, a family memory, a verb and finally a whole archive.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：颗粒失去能量而落下，这一次沉降随后变成一层、一份载荷、一份酒渣、一段家族记忆、一个动词，最后成为一整部档案。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: grains falling through still water and coming to rest on the bottom.
core.cn: 核心意象：颗粒穿过静水落下，停在底部。

branches.en: SETTLING: the physical act is the same in a river, a kettle and a jar.
branches.cn: 沉降：河、壶、瓶中的物理动作相同。

branches.en: LAYER UPON LAYER: one band is an event, and the whole stack is an archive.
branches.cn: 层层相叠：一层是一次事件，整叠则是一部档案。

branches.en: ON THE MOVE: before it settles, the same material is a suspended load and a water-quality problem.
branches.cn: 搬运之中：在沉降之前，同样的物质是悬移质，也是水质问题。

branches.en: IN A BOTTLE: wine lees are the same settling seen in a kitchen.
branches.cn: 瓶中：酒渣是同一沉降在厨房里的样子。

branches.en: FROM NOUN TO VERB AND TO MEMORY: what settles can be laid down deliberately, or remembered slowly.
branches.cn: 从名词到动词与记忆：沉下的东西可以被有意堆积，也可以被缓慢记住。

intro.en: Sediment is built from a Latin verb plus a result suffix, and both pieces recur across a large English family.
intro.cn: sediment 由拉丁动词加结果后缀构成，这两部分在英语的大家族中反复出现。

latinIntro.en: Latin sedere 'to sit' gives sediment, session, resident, sedentary and sedative; -mentum marks the result of an action, as in monumentum and argumentum.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 sedere「坐」衍生 sediment、session、resident、sedentary 与 sedative；-mentum 标记动作结果，如 monumentum 与 argumentum。

definition_zh: 种子；起因；播种；种子选手
definition_en: the small part of a plant from which a new plant grows, the origin of a feeling or situation, to plant seeds, or a ranked player in a tournament
core_image: 掌心摊开几粒小小的褐色种子，外壳上还沾着泥土
scene: 春天一到，他把种子埋进松软的土里。They planted the seed in early spring.

senses.title: Plant seed
senses.definition: the small hard part of a plant that can grow into a new plant
senses.definitionCN: 植物中能长出新生植株的坚硬小部分
senses.example: She planted seeds in small pots.
senses.exampleCN: 她把种子种在小花盆里。
senses.why: This is the everyday botanical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是日常的植物学义。

senses.title: Origin
senses.definition: the beginning or cause of something
senses.definitionCN: 某事的开端或起因
senses.example: The remark planted the seed of doubt.
senses.exampleCN: 那句话种下了怀疑的种子。
senses.why: An idea that will grow is pictured as a seed.
senses.whyCN: 将要生长起来的想法被比作种子。

senses.title: Plant seeds
senses.definition: to plant seeds in the ground
senses.definitionCN: 把种子播进土里
senses.example: Farmers seed the fields in April.
senses.exampleCN: 农民在四月给田地播种。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb for sowing.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为表示播种的动词。

senses.title: Ranked player
senses.definition: a player ranked so as not to meet other top players early
senses.definitionCN: 被排定名次、以免过早与其他高手相遇的选手
senses.example: He is the top seed in the tournament.
senses.exampleCN: 他是本次比赛的头号种子。
senses.why: Tournaments seed players like plants in ordered rows.
senses.whyCN: 赛事像分行播种一样给选手排位。

intro.en: Seed comes from Old English sæd, from a Germanic root for sowing.

items.en: Sæd meant that which is sown.
items.cn: sæd 意为被播下的东西。

items.en: The word also covered offspring and origin.
items.cn: 该词也涵盖后代与起源。

items.cn: seed 同时保留植物与起源两种含义。

items.en: The verb grew from the noun.
items.cn: 动词义由名词义发展而来。

items.en: Sport gave the word its ranked-player sense.
items.cn: 体育又赋予它「种子选手」的义项。

definition_zh: 寻找；寻求；试图

senses.definitionCN: 试图找到某人或某物

senses.exampleCN: 她到处寻找丢失的钥匙。

items.example: We seek a quiet place to rest.

He is seeking a new challenge.

items.meaning: a person who looks for something

求职者在办公室外排队。
他活像个追求享乐的人。

definition_zh: 部分；片段；细分市场；分割
definition_en: one of the parts into which something divides, a short piece of speech or writing, a group of customers with similar needs, or to divide something into parts
core_image: 一只橘子被一瓣瓣掰开，摆在木桌上
scene: 她把橘子一瓣瓣掰开，分给围坐的孩子。She divided the orange into segments.

senses.title: Natural part
senses.definition: one of the parts into which something naturally divides
senses.definitionCN: 某物自然分成的若干部分之一
senses.example: The orange breaks into easy segments.
senses.exampleCN: 这只橘子很容易分成一瓣瓣。
senses.why: Fruit and animals have natural segments.
senses.whyCN: 水果与动物都有天然的分节部分。

senses.title: Piece of speech
senses.definition: a short piece of speech or writing
senses.definitionCN: 口头或书面材料中的一小段
senses.example: She repeated a segment of the interview.
senses.exampleCN: 她重复了采访中的一个片段。
senses.why: A broadcast or text is cut into segments.
senses.whyCN: 广播或文本常被切分成若干片段。

senses.title: Market group
senses.definition: a group of customers with similar needs
senses.definitionCN: 需求相似的顾客群体
senses.example: The ad targets a young segment.
senses.exampleCN: 这则广告针对年轻群体。
senses.why: Marketers split buyers into segments.
senses.whyCN: 营销者把买家划分成不同细分群体。

senses.title: Divide
senses.definition: to divide something into parts
senses.definitionCN: 把某物分成若干部分
senses.example: The company segmented its market.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司细分了自己的市场。
senses.why: The noun became a verb meaning to split.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为表示切分的动词。

intro.en: Segment comes from Latin segmentum, a cutting, from secare, to cut.
intro.cn: segment 源自拉丁语 segmentum（切下之物），出自 secare（切）。

items.en: Secare meant to cut.
items.cn: secare 意为切。

items.en: Segmentum named a piece cut off.
items.cn: segmentum 指切下来的一块。

items.en: English used segment for a geometric part.
items.cn: 英语用 segment 指几何上的一段。

items.en: The word spread to speech and biology.
items.cn: 该词扩展到言语与生物学领域。

items.en: Business adopted it for market groups.
items.cn: 商业领域用它指市场细分群体。

note.en: Segment is compared with similar-looking words and with words for parts.
note.cn: 把 segment 与形近词以及表示部分的词作比较。

entries.definition: relating to segments
divided into segments
the act of dividing into parts
one of the parts of something
a part of an economy or area
a share of something

normalIntro.en: Segment means a piece cut or divided from a whole.
normalIntro.cn: segment 意为从整体中切分出来的一块。

normal.en: An orange is easy to split into segments.
normal.cn: 橘子很容易分成一瓣瓣。

normal.en: A line segment has two endpoints.
normal.cn: 线段有两个端点。

normal.en: A radio show is made of segments.
normal.cn: 广播节目由若干片段组成。

normal.en: Marketers divide buyers into segments.
normal.cn: 营销者把买家分成细分群体。

normal.en: Segment shares the root sect, meaning cut.
normal.cn: segment 与表示「切」的词根 sect 同源。

abstract.en: Every whole can be seen as a set of segments.
abstract.cn: 每个整体都可以看作若干部分。

abstract.en: A segment is meaningful only against its whole.
abstract.cn: 一个片段只有对照整体才有意义。

abstract.en: Choosing your segment changes what you see.
abstract.cn: 选择哪个片段，会改变你看到的东西。

examples.en: The orange breaks into easy segments.
examples.cn: 这只橘子很容易分成一瓣瓣。

examples.en: She repeated a segment of the interview.

examples.en: The ad targets a young segment.
examples.cn: 这则广告针对年轻群体。

dict_mnemonic.text: segment 由拉丁词干 seg（切）加 -ment 构成，本义「切下的一块」，引申为部分、片段与市场细分。

root: 源自拉丁语 segmentum（切下的一块），出自 secare（切），核心义「切分出来的一段」。

sensesIntro.en: Segment means a natural part, a piece of speech, a market group, or to divide.
sensesIntro.cn: segment 意为部分、片段、细分群体或分割。

core.en: A piece separated from a larger whole.
core.cn: 从更大整体中分离出来的一块。

branches.en: A natural division of fruit or body.
branches.cn: 水果或身体天然的分节部分。

branches.en: A short piece of talk or text.
branches.cn: 讲话或文本的一小段。

branches.en: A group of similar customers.
branches.cn: 需求相似的一群顾客。

branches.en: The act of splitting into parts.
branches.cn: 把整体切成部分的动作。

branches.cn: 名词与动词共享同一个「切分」意象。

items.example: Each segment of the pipe fits tightly.

items.example: The worm has a segmental body.

items.exampleCN: 市场细分指导着这项计划。

items.exampleCN: 这个社会具有分段结构。

items.example: They dissect a fish in class.

items.example: The lines intersect at a point.
Bisect the square with a line.

definition_zh: 隔离；分开；按类别分开（垃圾、材料等）；（基因）分离；把（病人）单独隔开
definition_en: to set people or things apart into separate groups, either by policy, by sorting or by a natural process
core_image: 牧人举着木杖，把混在一起的羊群赶向左右两道栏门
scene: 牧人把混在一起的羊群分成两路，一路进左栏，一路进右栏。An old rule used to segregate passengers by race on the same bus.
sceneCN: 这里指「按种族把人群强制分开」（第 1 个义项：按群体实行隔离）；句意为旧时的规定在同一辆公交车上按种族把乘客隔开。可辨识物件：木杖、羊栏、栏门、公交车、座位。

pos.zh: 被隔离的（少用，多见于技术文献）

senses.title: Separate people by group
senses.definition: to require different racial, ethnic or social groups to use separate places, services or institutions
senses.definitionCN: 要求不同种族、族裔或社会群体使用分开的场所、服务或机构
senses.example: Old rules segregated passengers by race on the same bus.
senses.exampleCN: 旧规定在同一辆公交车上按种族把乘客隔开。
senses.why: The Latin verb means 'to separate from the herd', and the modern racial use applies that herding action to people.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「把……从畜群中分开」，现代种族用法把这个分群动作用于人。

senses.title: Sort materials into streams
senses.definition: to separate waste, recycling or components into categories before further handling
senses.definitionCN: 在进一步处理之前，把垃圾、回收物或零件按类别分开
senses.example: Households that segregate waste at the source raise the quality of recycling.
senses.exampleCN: 在源头把垃圾分类的家庭提高了回收质量。
senses.why: The act of driving one part away from the rest works just as well for glass, paper and food scraps.
senses.whyCN: 把一部分从其余部分赶开的动作，用在玻璃、纸张与厨余上同样合适。

senses.title: Alleles parting in meiosis
senses.titleCN: 等位基因在减数分裂中分离
senses.definition: to separate paired alleles so that each gamete receives a single copy
senses.definitionCN: 使成对的等位基因分开，让每个配子只得到一份
senses.example: During meiosis, homologous chromosomes segregate into different gametes.
senses.exampleCN: 在减数分裂中，同源染色体分离进入不同的配子。
senses.why: Chromosomes part into two sets as cleanly as a herd is split between two pens.
senses.whyCN: 染色体分成两组，干净利落得就像羊群被分进两栏。

senses.title: Keep an infected patient apart
senses.definition: to place a patient or case in isolation to prevent contact with others
senses.definitionCN: 把病人或病例单独安置，以防止与他人接触
senses.example: The hospital segregated the patient until the test results returned.
senses.exampleCN: 医院把病人单独隔离，直到检测结果出来。
senses.why: Medical separation borrows the fencing image: one body is kept in its own pen for the safety of the herd.
senses.whyCN: 医学隔离借用了围栏意象：为了群体的安全，把一个身体关进自己的栏里。

senses.title: Put a group in a separate space
senses.titleCN: 把一群人安置在另一处空间
senses.definition: to assign a group to a distinct room, building or area rather than a shared one
senses.definitionCN: 把某个群体分配到单独的教室、建筑或区域，而非共享空间
senses.example: The school used to segregate younger pupils into a separate wing.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学校过去把低年级学生分到单独的一翼。
senses.why: A building, like a pasture, can be divided by walls; the verb marks which side each group is sent to.
senses.whyCN: 建筑和牧场一样可以用墙分开；这个动词标记每个群体被送往哪一边。

senses.title: Split duties between people
senses.definition: to divide authority over a transaction so that no single person controls the whole process
senses.definitionCN: 把同一笔交易的权限分开，使没有一个人控制全过程
senses.example: The finance office segregates duties so that the same clerk cannot approve and pay.
senses.exampleCN: 财务部门把职责分开，使同一名职员不能既批准又付款。
senses.why: Internal control uses the verb because separating tasks prevents one hand from owning the whole path.
senses.whyCN: 内部控制使用这个动词，因为把任务分开可以防止一只手掌握整条路径。

senses.title: Separate oneself from a group
senses.titleCN: 把自己从群体中分出来
senses.definition: to withdraw deliberately from a group or from shared activity
senses.definitionCN: 有意从一个群体或共同活动中退出
senses.example: He segregated himself from the planning group after the dispute.
senses.exampleCN: 争执之后，他把自己从筹备组中分离出来。
senses.why: Turning the verb on oneself shows that the pen can be entered by choice as well as by force.
senses.whyCN: 把动词转向自己，说明栏门既可以被人强行关上，也可以由自己走进去。

senses.title: Atoms gathering in an alloy
senses.definition: to redistribute unevenly within a solid, so that regions differ in composition
senses.definitionCN: 在固体内部不均匀地重新分布，使各区域成分不同
senses.example: Carbon atoms segregate along the grain boundaries as the steel cools.
senses.exampleCN: 钢冷却时，碳原子沿晶界偏聚。
senses.why: In materials science the herd image becomes literal again: like atoms gather into their own flock.
senses.whyCN: 在材料科学中，畜群意象又变回字面：同类原子聚成自己的群。

intro.en: Segregate comes from Latin segregare 'to separate from the flock', built on se- 'apart' and grex, gregis 'flock, herd'. The English verb appeared in the sixteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: segregate 来自拉丁 segregare「把……从羊群中分开」，由 se-「分开」与 grex（属格 gregis）「羊群、畜群」构成。英语动词在十六世纪出现。年代均为约数。

items.en: Grex meant 'flock, herd, crowd'. Its deeper origin is not established; the herd root proposed for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: grex 意为「羊群、畜群、人群」。其更深来源未得到证明；为它提出的「畜群」词根属于重构形式。

items.en: Se- 'apart' plus the verb from grex produced segregare, 'to set apart from the herd'.
items.cn: se-「分开」加由 grex 构成的动词，产生 segregare「把……从畜群中分出」。

items.en: The verb entered English in the sixteenth century with the general sense of setting things or people apart.
items.cn: 这个动词在十六世纪进入英语，泛指把事物或人分开。

items.en: By the nineteenth and twentieth centuries the verb was used for official separation of racial groups, especially in the United States.
items.cn: 到十九与二十世纪，这个动词用于官方按种族分开群体，尤其在美国。

items.en: Genetics adopted the verb for the parting of alleles, and metallurgy for the uneven gathering of atoms.
items.cn: 遗传学借用这个动词指等位基因的分离，冶金学则用它指原子的不均匀聚集。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin and first date): the pre-Latin source of grex is unsettled, and no exact first citation is fixed for the racial use, so dates here are approximations.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源与首见年代）：grex 在拉丁语之前的来源无定论，种族用法的最早书证也不确定，因此这里给出的年代均为约数。

note.en: Group one holds the same flock-root family; group two holds verbs that divide by other means.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「畜群」词根的词族；第二组是用其他方式划分的动词。

entries.definition: The system or result of keeping groups apart; the verb names the act that produces it.
entries.definitionCN: 把群体隔开的制度或结果；动词指产生它的动作。

entries.definition: Describing something already kept apart, as a segregated carriage or school.
entries.definitionCN: 描述已被隔开的事物，如隔离车厢或隔离学校。

entries.definition: A person who advocates separation of groups; it names a supporter, not the act.
entries.definitionCN: 主张分开群体的人；指支持者，而非动作。

entries.definition: Means sociable and living in groups; it shares the herd noun but carries no idea of separation.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「群居的、爱社交的」；共享「畜群」名词，却不含分离之意。

entries.definition: To divide or keep apart; segregate usually adds a group, a rule or a systematic policy.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指分开或保持分离；segregate 通常还带有群体、规则或系统政策的含义。

entries.definition: To place something entirely alone or apart from contact; it stresses total separation rather than group sorting.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物完全单独放置或切断接触；强调彻底分离，而非群体分类。

entries.definition: To arrange things by category, often for practical handling; it is neutral and lacks the social weight of segregate.
entries.definitionCN: 按类别整理物品，通常为了实际处理；它中立，没有 segregate 的社会重量。

entries.definition: To break a whole into parts; it does not imply that the parts are kept from meeting again.
entries.definitionCN: 把整体分成部分；不暗示各部分此后被阻止再度接触。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real herding verb, the real derivatives and the real technical phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的分群动词、真实的派生词与真实的技术搭配。

normal.en: The Latin verb means 'to drive part of the herd away', so the English verb keeps the image of a gate closing between two pens.
normal.cn: 拉丁动词意为「把一部分羊赶出群」，因此英语动词保留了两栏之间关门上锁的意象。

normal.en: The family runs segregate, segregated, segregation, segregationist, segregative and segregational.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 segregate、segregated、segregation、segregationist、segregative 与 segregational。

normal.en: The social phrases are segregate by race and segregate the sexes.
normal.cn: 社会搭配有按种族隔离与把两性分开。

normal.en: The technical phrases are segregate waste, segregate duties and segregate alleles.
normal.cn: 技术搭配有垃圾分类、职责分离与等位基因分离。

normal.en: The same herd noun appears in gregarious, which describes animals that stay together instead of being parted.
normal.cn: 同一个「畜群」名词出现在 gregarious 中，那个词描述结群而不被分开的动物。

abstract.en: Picture a wooden gate shutting between two pens while the animals on each side stop calling to each other.
abstract.cn: 想象两栏之间的木门关上，两边的动物不再互相呼唤。

abstract.en: Picture three bins with lids of different colours, each taking only one stream.
abstract.cn: 想象三只桶盖着不同颜色的盖子，每只只收一种物料。

abstract.en: Picture two clerks sitting at separate desks so that neither can finish the payment alone.
abstract.cn: 想象两名职员坐在分开的桌前，谁也无法独自完成付款。

examples.en: The city council finally stopped segregating students by neighbourhood income.
examples.cn: 市议会终于停止按街区收入把学生分开。

examples.en: Nurses segregate infectious cases in a separate ward.
examples.cn: 护士把传染病例隔离在单独的病房。

examples.en: As the alloy cooled, tin began to segregate at the surface.
examples.cn: 合金冷却时，锡开始在表面偏聚。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「分开」加「羊群」——把混在一起的羊赶进两道栏门 → 隔离、分开

root: segregate 来自拉丁 segregare「把……从羊群中分开」= se-「分开」+ grex（属格 gregis）「羊群、畜群」。grex 在拉丁语之前的更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one action: a part is driven away from the rest. The action is applied to races, waste, alleles, a patient, a group in a building, office duties, the self and atoms in a metal.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：把一部分从其余部分赶开。这个动作依次用于种族、垃圾、等位基因、病人、建筑中的群体、办公职责、自己以及金属中的原子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a herder dividing the flock with a raised staff.
core.cn: 核心意象：牧人举起木杖，把羊群分成两路。

branches.en: THE FORCED PEN: the racial sense closes the gate on people who did not choose it.
branches.cn: 强制分栏：种族义对那些并未选择的人关上栏门。

branches.en: THE SORTING BIN: materials are separated so that mixing does not undo their value.
branches.cn: 分类桶：把物料分开，使混杂不至于毁掉它们的价值。

branches.en: THE GENETIC PEN: chromosomes part into two sets as cleanly as animals into two pens.
branches.cn: 基因分栏：染色体分成两组，和动物分进两栏一样干净。

branches.en: THE SEPARATE ROOM: a patient or a group is moved behind a wall for safety or order.
branches.cn: 分隔的房间：病人或群体被移到墙后，以求安全或秩序。

branches.en: THE GUARDED PATH: duties, the self and atoms are all kept apart so that no single part controls the whole.
branches.cn: 受守护的路径：职责、自己与原子都被分开，使任何单独部分都无法掌控整体。

intro.en: The verb can be read from a Latin prefix of separation, a Latin noun for a herd, the derived verb and its family.
intro.cn: 这个动词可以按表示分离的拉丁前缀、表示畜群的拉丁名词、由它们构成的动词以及词族逐段读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin se- and grex give segregare, segregate and segregation; the same herd noun also yields gregarious.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 se- 与 grex 衍生 segregare、segregate 与 segregation；同一个「畜群」名词还衍生 gregarious。

items.example: The prefix marks departure from the group.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标记离开群体。

items.example: The noun gives the image of animals kept together.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词提供动物结群的意象。

items.example: The Latin verb named the act of setting one part aside.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁动词指把一部分放到一旁的动作。

items.example: The rule segregated passengers by race.
items.exampleCN: 这项规定按种族把乘客隔开。

items.example: The ward was segregated from the rest of the hospital.
items.exampleCN: 这间病房与医院其余部分隔开。

items.example: The segregationist blocked the new admissions rule.
items.exampleCN: 主张隔离的人阻挠了新的招生规定。

items.example: The tax had a segregative effect on the housing market.
items.exampleCN: 这项税对住房市场产生了分离效果。

items.example: The seals are gregarious on the rocks.
items.exampleCN: 这些海豹在礁石上成群结队。

derivatives.meaning: the act or system of separation

definition_zh: 地震的；地震引起的；震动的；影响巨大的
definition_en: relating to earthquakes or to the vibrations they send through the ground
core_image: 一条波线从地底某一点向四面扩散，经过之处墙体和地表都在轻微起伏
scene: 地震台网的值班室里，屏幕上一条波形刚刚越过警戒线。 Sensors across the valley recorded seismic activity for three minutes.
sceneCN: 这里 seismic 是「地震的」（第 1 个义项：与地震或地震引起的震动有关）；句意为谷地各处的传感器记录了三分钟的地震活动。

pos.zh: 地震的；地震引起的；震动的；影响巨大的

derivatives.zh: 地震活动性；某地区的地震频度
在地震方面；按抗震方式
地震学（seismo- 组合形式参与构成的学科名）

senses.title: Relating to earthquakes
senses.definition: connected with earthquakes or with the shaking of the earth's crust
senses.definitionCN: 与地震或地壳震动相关的
senses.example: Sensors across the valley recorded seismic activity for three minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 谷地各处的传感器记录了三分钟的地震活动。
senses.why: seismic comes from Greek seismos, a shaking or earthquake, so the adjective simply points to that event.
senses.whyCN: seismic 来自希腊 seismos「震动、地震」，因此这个形容词直接指向那个事件。

senses.title: Concerning seismic waves
senses.definition: describing the elastic waves that travel through rock after a sudden rupture
senses.definitionCN: 描述岩体突然破裂后在岩石中传播的弹性波
senses.example: Seismic waves arrive from the focus in several distinct phases.
senses.exampleCN: 地震波以几个不同震相从震源抵达。
senses.why: once instruments could record the shaking, the adjective was attached to the waves that carry it, not only to the event.
senses.whyCN: 当仪器能记录震动之后，这个形容词就不仅指事件，也用于承载震动的波。

senses.title: Monitoring ground motion
senses.definition: used for instruments, networks or data that detect and measure ground shaking
senses.definitionCN: 用于探测与测量地面震动的仪器、台网或数据
senses.example: The seismic network sent an alert before the strongest shaking arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 地震台网在最强震动到达前发出了警报。
senses.why: a monitoring system is named by what it watches, so seismic became the standard label for earthquake detection.
senses.whyCN: 监测系统按它监视的对象命名，因此 seismic 成了地震探测的标准标签。

senses.title: Imaging the ground by sound
senses.definition: relating to the method that sends artificial vibrations into the ground and reads their echoes
senses.definitionCN: 与向地下发送人工震动并读取回波的方法有关
senses.example: A seismic survey mapped the salt dome under the seabed.
senses.exampleCN: 一次地震勘探测出了海床下的盐丘。
senses.why: the same physics that records earthquakes can be reversed: make a controlled shock and listen to the reflections.
senses.whyCN: 记录地震的同一套物理可以反用：制造可控震动，再听反射。

senses.title: Based on seismic data
senses.definition: derived from recorded ground motion, as in images of rock layers or fault maps
senses.definitionCN: 由记录到的地面运动推得，如岩层图像或断层图
senses.example: The seismic image shows a buried fault beneath the delta.
senses.exampleCN: 地震图像显示三角洲下有一条被掩埋的断层。
senses.why: data is named by the physical signal that produced it, so seismic became a shorthand for the whole imaging method.
senses.whyCN: 数据按产生它的物理信号命名，因此 seismic 成了整套成像方法的简称。

senses.title: Relating to earthquake risk
senses.definition: concerning the probability and expected strength of shaking at a place
senses.definitionCN: 关于某地发生震动的概率与预期强度
senses.example: The building code sets seismic requirements for every new school.
senses.exampleCN: 建筑规范为每所新建学校规定了抗震要求。
senses.why: risk language uses the adjective because the hazard itself is the shaking, not the fault line on a map.
senses.whyCN: 风险语言使用这个形容词，因为危险本身是震动，而不是地图上的断层线。

senses.title: Designed to resist earthquakes
senses.definition: built or fitted so that structures can survive strong shaking
senses.definitionCN: 为使结构能在强烈震动中存留而建造或装配
senses.example: Seismic isolation lets the base move while the floors stay steady.
senses.exampleCN: 地震隔震让底座移动而楼层保持稳定。
senses.why: engineering turns the adjective into a design goal: whatever resists the shaking is called seismic.
senses.whyCN: 工程学把这个形容词变成设计目标：凡是能抵御震动的都冠以 seismic。

senses.title: Figuratively enormous in effect
senses.titleCN: 比喻：影响如同地震般巨大的
senses.definition: having an effect as sudden and far-reaching as an earthquake
senses.definitionCN: 产生的影响如地震般突然而深远
senses.example: The ruling caused a seismic shift in how the industry was financed.
senses.exampleCN: 这项裁决使该行业的融资方式发生了地震般的转变。
senses.why: the figurative sense borrows the scale of an earthquake: not just a change, but one that rearranges the ground under everything.
senses.whyCN: 比喻义借用了地震的规模：不只是变化，而是把一切脚下的地面重新排布。

intro.en: Seismic was formed in English in the nineteenth century from Greek seismos, a shaking, an earthquake, built on the verb seiein, to shake, plus the adjective suffix -ic. It has no Latin ancestor.
intro.cn: seismic 是 19 世纪英语新造词，来自希腊 seismos「震动、地震」，其词根为动词 seiein「摇动」，加形容词后缀 -ic。它没有拉丁语祖先。

items.en: Seiein meant to shake or drive by shaking. Its deeper pre-Greek origin is not established, so any Indo-European form for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: seiein 意为「摇动、以摇动驱使」。其希腊语之前的更深来源未获证明，因此为它给出的任何印欧形式都属重构。

items.en: Seismos named a shaking or an earthquake; the same stem appears in seismology and in older medical use for trembling.
items.cn: seismos 指一次震动或地震；同一词干也出现在 seismology，以及较早医学用语中的「颤抖」。

items.en: English scientists coined seismic in the mid nineteenth century to name the study and measurement of earthquakes, at a time when seismology was becoming a science.
items.cn: 19 世纪中叶，英语科学界造出 seismic，用来命名地震的研究与测量，当时地震学正成为一门科学。

items.en: In the twentieth century seismic survey came to mean deliberate sound-wave imaging of rock layers for oil, gas and engineering.
items.cn: 到 20 世纪，seismic survey 指为石油、天然气与工程目的，用声波对岩层做主动成像。

items.en: Late modern English extended the adjective to any change of earthquake scale, as in a seismic shift in policy or markets.
items.cn: 现代英语晚期把这个形容词扩展到任何地震级的变化，如政策或市场上的地震式转变。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin and first date): the pre-Greek root of seiein is unsettled, and the earliest printed use of seismic is dated only approximately to the 1850s.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源与首见年代）：seiein 的希腊语之前词根尚无定论，seismic 最早的印刷用例也只能约略定在 1850 年代。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same Greek shaking stem; group two holds adjectives that describe large earth movements or huge effects.
note.cn: 第一组是同出希腊「震动」词干的词；第二组是描述大规模地壳运动或巨大影响的形容词。

entries.definition: An older synonym meaning relating to an earthquake; it is now rare beside seismic.
entries.definitionCN: 较旧的同义词，意为「与地震有关的」；如今除 seismic 外已罕用。

entries.definition: Built with the Greek negative prefix a-: either free from earthquakes or designed to resist them.
entries.definitionCN: 由希腊否定前缀 a- 构成：或指无地震的，或指抗震的。

entries.definition: The frequency and distribution of earthquakes in a region; the noun behind seismic activity.
entries.definitionCN: 某地区地震的频度与分布；即 seismic activity 背后的名词。

entries.definition: Seismo- plus -graph, a writing instrument: the device that draws a record of ground motion.
entries.definitionCN: seismo- 加 -graph「书写」：把地面运动画成记录曲线的仪器。

entries.definition: Relating to the structure of the earth's crust and the plates that move it; tectonic events cause earthquakes but the word does not mean seismic.
entries.definitionCN: 与地壳结构及推动地壳的板块有关；构造事件会引发地震，但该词本身并不等于 seismic。

entries.definition: Literally shaking the earth, but in practice almost always figurative for enormously important; seismic covers both the literal and figurative.
entries.definitionCN: 字面为「摇动大地」，实际几乎总作比喻指「极其重大」；seismic 则兼具字面与比喻两义。

entries.definition: Relating to the physics of the earth as a whole, including gravity, magnetism and heat; seismic is only one branch of it.
entries.definitionCN: 与整个地球的物理有关，包括重力、磁场与热；seismic 只是其中一个分支。

entries.definition: Describing a disastrous outcome; it can describe an earthquake's effects but says nothing about shaking as such.
entries.definitionCN: 描述灾难性后果；可描述地震的影响，但本身并不指震动。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Greek seismos, shaking, plus -ic: the adjective of an earthquake.
normal.cn: 希腊 seismos「震动」加 -ic：地震的形容词。

normal.en: The family runs seismic, seismicity, aseismic, seismograph, seismometer, seismogram, seismology.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 seismic、seismicity、aseismic、seismograph、seismometer、seismogram、seismology。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: seismic wave, seismic survey, seismic hazard, seismic design.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：地震波、地震勘探、地震危险、抗震设计。

normal.en: seismo- is the combining form in instrument names, always tied to ground motion.
normal.cn: seismo- 是仪器名称中的组合形式，始终与地面运动相关。

normal.en: The figurative phrase seismic shift is a set expression for a very large change.
normal.cn: 比喻搭配 seismic shift 是「巨大转变」的固定说法。

abstract.en: Picture a stone dropped in a pond, but the rings run through rock.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗石子落入池塘，只是涟漪穿过的是岩石。

abstract.en: Picture a city where every table starts sliding at the same instant.
abstract.cn: 想象一座城市里每张桌子在同一瞬间开始滑动。

abstract.en: Picture a rulebook rewritten overnight while everyone is still asleep.
abstract.cn: 想象一本规则手册在众人熟睡时被一夜改写。

examples.en: The region has been quiet, with no seismic activity for a decade.
examples.cn: 该地区一直平静，十年来没有地震活动。

examples.en: Seismic reflection revealed a deep basin beneath the plain.
examples.cn: 地震反射探测揭示出平原之下有一个深盆地。

examples.en: The new evidence caused a seismic change in the accepted theory.
examples.cn: 新证据使公认理论发生了地震般的改变。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「seis（震）+ mic」——大地在抖动 → 地震的、震动的

root: 希腊 seismos「震动、地震」，源自 seiein「摇动」，加形容词后缀 -ic；希腊来源，无拉丁同族，拉丁词条留空。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow the same shaking: first the earthquake itself, then its waves, its monitoring, its use for imaging, its data, its risk, its engineering answer, and finally any change on the same scale.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一种震动展开：先是地震本身，继而它的波、监测、成像用途、数据、风险、工程对策，最后是任何同等规模的变化。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wave front spreading from one point underground, tilting everything it passes.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道波前从地下某点扩散，经过之处一切都在倾斜。

branches.en: THE EVENT: seismic points first at the earthquake itself.
branches.cn: 事件：seismic 首先指向地震本身。

branches.en: CARRYING AND WATCHING: waves carry the shaking, instruments watch it.
branches.cn: 承载与监视：波承载震动，仪器监视震动。

branches.en: ACTIVE USE: the same physics is turned into a lamp for the subsurface.
branches.cn: 主动利用：同一套物理被改造为照亮地下的灯。

branches.en: RISK AND RESPONSE: shaking becomes a design load to be resisted.
branches.cn: 风险与应对：震动变成必须抵御的设计荷载。

branches.en: METAPHOR: the scale of an earthquake is lent to social change.
branches.cn: 比喻：把地震的规模借给社会变化。

intro.en: Seismic is a Greek-derived adjective whose combining form seismo- appears at the front of a whole family of earth-science words.
intro.cn: seismic 是希腊来源的形容词，其组合形式 seismo- 出现在整族地球科学词汇的词首。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin ancestor: the family goes back to Greek seiein and seismos, and Latin gained only loanwords such as the medical use of tremor.
latinIntro.cn: 没有拉丁语祖先：这个词族上溯希腊 seiein 与 seismos；拉丁语只贡献了如医学用法的 tremor 等借词。

items.example: Seismo- heads the names of instruments and sciences.
items.exampleCN: seismo- 位于仪器与学科名称的词首。

items.example: The noun is the source of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是整个词族的来源。

items.example: The verb supplies the root sei-.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供词根 sei-。

items.example: The suffix makes an adjective from the noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把名词变成形容词。

items.meaning: the earthquake frequency of a region
items.example: Low seismicity made the site attractive.
items.exampleCN: 地震活动性低使该场址颇具吸引力。

items.example: The seismograph traced a long, low pulse.
items.exampleCN: 地震仪描出一条长而低的脉冲。

items.meaning: an instrument that measures ground motion
the record produced by a seismograph
items.exampleCN: 地震记录图显示两个到达震相。

items.example: Seismology grew from early earthquake catalogues.
items.exampleCN: 地震学从早期地震目录发展而来。

definition_zh: 地震学家；研究地震的科学家
definition_en: a scientist who studies earthquakes and the waves they send through the earth
core_image: 一位研究者俯身在长条记录纸前，用铅笔标出两条波线到达的时刻
scene: 老式地震观测台里，值班的人把刚到的记录纸压平在灯下。 The seismologist marked the arrival times of both phases on the record.
sceneCN: 这里 seismologist 是「地震学家」（第 1 个义项：以地震为研究对象的科学家）；句意为这位地震学家在记录图上标出两个震相的到达时刻。

senses.title: A scientist of earthquakes
senses.definition: a researcher whose subject is earthquakes, their causes and their effects
senses.definitionCN: 以地震、其成因与影响为研究对象的科研人员
senses.example: The seismologist marked the arrival times of both phases on the record.
senses.exampleCN: 这位地震学家在记录图上标出两个震相的到达时刻。
senses.why: seismologist is seismology plus -ist, the Greek suffix for a person who practises a craft or science.
senses.whyCN: seismologist 是 seismology 加 -ist，后者是希腊语中表示从事某技艺或科学之人的后缀。

senses.title: An analyst of a seismic network
senses.definition: a person who runs or reads the output of a network of monitoring stations
senses.definitionCN: 运行或解读监测台网输出的人员
senses.example: The network seismologist spotted a gap in the data at once.
senses.exampleCN: 台网地震学家立刻发现了数据中的一个缺口。
senses.why: a science built on continuous recording needs people who watch the stream, and they take the same professional name.
senses.whyCN: 建立在连续记录之上的科学需要有人盯着数据流，这些人也用同一个职业名称。

senses.title: A reader of seismograms
senses.definition: a specialist who locates an event and estimates its size from recorded traces
senses.definitionCN: 根据记录曲线定位事件并估算其大小的专业人员
senses.example: A seismologist fixed the depth of the focus within a minute.
senses.exampleCN: 一位地震学家在一分钟内定出了震源深度。
senses.why: the trace is the primary evidence, so the person who can read it is named by the discipline rather than by the instrument.
senses.whyCN: 记录曲线是首要证据，因此能读懂它的人按学科而非按仪器命名。

senses.title: A field instrument deployer
senses.definition: a scientist who installs and services stations in remote or temporary sites
senses.definitionCN: 在偏远或临时场地安装并维护台站的科研人员
senses.example: The field seismologist carried three sensors up the ridge.
senses.exampleCN: 野外地震工作者把三台传感器背上了山脊。
senses.why: field marks the branch that leaves the observatory, but the title still comes from the shared discipline.
senses.whyCN: field 标出离开观测台的那一支，但头衔仍来自共同学科。

senses.title: An exploration seismologist
senses.definition: a specialist who uses controlled seismic sources to image rock for industry
senses.definitionCN: 用可控震源为工业目的给岩层成像的专家
senses.example: The exploration seismologist picked the salt boundary by hand.
senses.exampleCN: 勘探地震学家手工拾取了盐层边界。
senses.why: the same training serves a commercial goal, and the compound title records that shift of purpose.
senses.whyCN: 同样的训练服务于商业目标，复合头衔记录了这一用途转变。

senses.title: A planetary seismologist
senses.definition: a scientist who applies seismic methods to the Moon, Mars or other solid bodies
senses.definitionCN: 把地震方法用于月球、火星或其他固态天体的科学家
senses.example: A planetary seismologist compared moonquakes with terrestrial ones.
senses.exampleCN: 一位行星地震学家把月震与地球地震作了比较。
senses.why: planet names the object rather than the method, showing that the profession travels with the instrument.
senses.whyCN: planet 指对象而非方法，说明这一职业随仪器一起旅行。

senses.title: An engineering seismologist
senses.definition: a specialist who turns seismic hazard into values used for structural design
senses.definitionCN: 把地震危险转化为结构设计所用参数的专家
senses.example: The engineering seismologist supplied the design spectrum for the bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 工程地震学家提供了这座桥的设计反应谱。
senses.why: engineering marks the branch whose output is a number a builder can use, not a paper.
senses.whyCN: engineering 标出这样一支：它的产出是建造者能用的数字，而不是论文。

senses.title: A historical seismologist
senses.definition: a researcher who reconstructs past earthquakes from old records, diaries and damage reports
senses.definitionCN: 从旧记录、日记与灾害报告中重建过去地震的研究者
senses.example: The historical seismologist found a quake missing from every catalogue.
senses.exampleCN: 这位历史地震学家发现了一次在所有目录中都缺失的地震。
senses.why: history marks the branch that reads paper rather than rock, yet asks the same question about the same event.
senses.whyCN: history 标出读纸而非读岩的那一支，但它对同一事件提出同样的问题。

intro.en: Seismologist is seismology plus -ist, a Greek-derived agent suffix. The base goes back to Greek seismos, earthquake, and -logia, study. The whole word is a modern English formation with no Latin ancestor.
intro.cn: seismologist 是 seismology 加 -ist，后者是希腊来源的施事后缀。词基上溯希腊 seismos「地震」与 -logia「研究」。整个词是近代英语构词，没有拉丁语祖先。

items.en: Seismos, a shaking or earthquake, comes from seiein, to shake. The pre-Greek root is unattested and any older form is reconstructed.
items.cn: seismos「震动、地震」来自 seiein「摇动」。其希腊语之前的词根没有实证，任何更早形式均属重构。

items.en: The suffix -istes named a person engaged in an action or profession, and it reaches English as -ist in scientist, geologist and seismologist.
items.cn: 后缀 -istes 指从事某动作或职业的人，进入英语作 -ist，见于 scientist、geologist 与 seismologist。

items.en: As seismology took shape in the 1850s, seismologist appeared for the people who measured and catalogued earthquakes.
items.cn: 随着地震学在 1850 年代成形，seismologist 出现，指测量与编目地震的人。

items.en: In the twentieth century compounds such as field, exploration, engineering and planetary seismologist marked new workplaces for the same training.
items.cn: 到 20 世纪，field、exploration、engineering、planetary 等复合头衔标出同样训练所去的新工作场所。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date only): the earliest printed use of seismologist is not precisely dated and is usually placed in the second half of the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代）：seismologist 最早的印刷用例没有精确年代，通常被定在 19 世纪后半叶。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same stem that differ only in suffix; group two holds neighbouring earth-science professions.
note.cn: 第一组是同出词干、只差后缀的词；第二组是相邻的地球科学职业。

entries.definition: The science itself; -logy names the field, while -ist names the person who works in it.
entries.definitionCN: 学科本身；-logy 命名领域，-ist 命名在其中工作的人。

entries.definition: Relating to seismology, as in seismological observatory; it describes things, not people.
entries.definitionCN: 与地震学有关，如地震观测台；描述事物，不描述人。

entries.definition: The paper or digital trace a seismologist reads; it is the object, not the reader.
entries.definitionCN: 地震学家所读的纸质或数字曲线；是对象，不是读者。

entries.definition: The sensor that measures motion; -meter marks a device, in contrast with the person suffix -ist.
entries.definitionCN: 测量运动的传感器；-meter 标记装置，与表人的 -ist 形成对照。

entries.definition: A scientist of the earth's physical properties in general; a seismologist is one kind of geophysicist.
entries.definitionCN: 研究地球物理性质的总称；地震学家是地球物理学家的一种。

entries.definition: A scientist of rocks and strata; the two overlap in the field but study different evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 研究岩石与地层的科学家；两者在野外有交集，但所研究的证据不同。

entries.definition: A specialist in volcanoes; often works beside a seismologist because moving magma produces tremor.
entries.definitionCN: 研究火山的专家；常与地震学家并肩工作，因为岩浆运移会产生颤动。

entries.definition: A general description of someone who works at an observatory; it does not claim scientific training in seismology.
entries.definitionCN: 对在观测台工作者的泛称；并不表示受过地震学的科学训练。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: seismology + -ist: the person who practises the study of earthquakes.
normal.cn: seismology + -ist：从事地震研究的人。

normal.en: The title set runs seismologist, seismologists, seismology, seismological, seismologically.
normal.cn: 头衔词族包括 seismologist、seismologists、seismology、seismological、seismologically。

normal.en: Specialist compounds: field, exploration, engineering, planetary and historical seismologist.
normal.cn: 专业复合词：野外、勘探、工程、行星与历史地震学家。

normal.en: The instrument words end in -graph, -meter, -gram; the person word ends in -ist.
normal.cn: 仪器词以 -graph、-meter、-gram 结尾；表人的词以 -ist 结尾。

normal.en: News usage fixes the phrase: seismologists estimate the magnitude within minutes.
normal.cn: 新闻用法固定了搭配：地震学家在几分钟内估算震级。

abstract.en: Picture a translator who listens to the ground and writes down what it said.
abstract.cn: 想象一位译者，听取大地的声音，再把它写下。

abstract.en: Picture a detective arriving after the event and reading the damage as testimony.
abstract.cn: 想象一位侦探在事件之后赶到，把破坏读成证词。

abstract.en: Picture a lighthouse keeper, except the light is pointed inward at the planet.
abstract.cn: 想象一位灯塔看守，只是灯不是向外照，而是照向行星内部。

examples.en: The seismologist on duty called the emergency office before the shaking reached the city.
examples.cn: 值班地震学家在震动抵达城市之前打电话给了应急部门。

examples.en: A seismologist can tell a quarry blast from a natural quake by the trace.
examples.cn: 地震学家能从记录曲线上分辨采石场爆破与天然地震。

examples.en: The team included a seismologist, a geologist and two engineers.
examples.cn: 团队包括一位地震学家、一位地质学家和两位工程师。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「seismo（地震）+ logist（学者）」——研究地震的学者 → 地震学家

root: 希腊 seismos「地震」+ -logia「研究」+ -istes「从事……的人」→ 英语 seismologist。希腊来源，无拉丁同族，拉丁词条留空。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one profession through its workplaces: the researcher, the network analyst, the trace reader, the field hand, the exploration hand, the planetary hand, the engineering hand and the historian of old paper.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟随同一职业走过不同工作场所：研究者、台网分析员、曲线解读者、野外人员、勘探人员、行星人员、工程人员，以及读旧纸的历史研究者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person bent over a long paper strip, pencil in hand, marking the exact moment a wave arrived.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人俯身在长条纸带前，手握铅笔，标出波到达的准确时刻。

branches.en: CORE SKILL: reading the record and turning it into an event with place, depth and size.
branches.cn: 核心技能：读记录，并把它转成带有位置、深度与大小的事件。

branches.en: WATCHING THE STREAM: the network analyst keeps the record continuous.
branches.cn: 盯住数据流：台网分析员让记录保持连续。

branches.en: LEAVING THE BUILDING: the field worker carries the instrument to where the signal is.
branches.cn: 走出大楼：野外人员把仪器背到信号所在之处。

branches.en: OTHER GOALS AND OTHER WORLDS: the same training serves industry or another planet.
branches.cn: 别的目标与别的世界：同样的训练服务工业，或服务另一颗行星。

branches.en: SERVICE AND MEMORY: one turns hazard into design values, the other recovers forgotten events.
branches.cn: 服务与记忆：一个把危险变成设计参数，一个找回被遗忘的事件。

intro.en: Seismologist is a three-part build: an earthquake stem, a study suffix and a person suffix, all from Greek.
intro.cn: seismologist 由三部分构成：「地震」词干、「研究」后缀与「人」后缀，全部来自希腊语。

latinIntro.en: No Latin element enters the word; Latin appears only in the later language of scientific publication.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词里没有拉丁成分；拉丁语只出现在后来作为科学出版语言的层面。

items.example: Seismo- names the subject of the profession.
items.exampleCN: seismo- 点明这一职业的研究对象。

items.example: The noun reaches English through scientific borrowing.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词经科学借词进入英语。

items.example: -Logy turns the subject into a discipline.
items.exampleCN: -logy 把研究对象变成一门学科。

items.example: -Ist turns the discipline into a profession.
The seismologist checked the station log.
items.exampleCN: 地震学家核对了台站日志。

items.example: The seismological staff meets each morning.
items.exampleCN: 地震学人员每天早晨开会。

items.example: The seismograph ran on a clockwork drum.
items.exampleCN: 那台地震仪靠发条滚筒运转。

items.meaning: the record produced by the instrument
items.example: The seismogram is the primary evidence.
items.exampleCN: 地震记录图是首要证据。

items.meaningCN: 测量地面运动的传感器
items.example: The seismometer needs a level base.

definition_zh: 地震学；研究地震与地震波的学科
definition_en: the scientific study of earthquakes and of the waves they send through the earth
core_image: 一间地下观测室里，滚筒纸带不断走动，把来自地底的每一次轻微抖动画成曲线
scene: 大学地质系的地下观测室里，学生围着一台持续走纸的滚筒记录仪。 She chose seismology because she wanted to understand what happens miles below the surface.
sceneCN: 这里 seismology 是「地震学」（第 1 个义项：以地震为研究对象的学科）；句意为她选择地震学，是因为想弄清楚地表以下数英里处发生了什么。

forms.label: 复数（指多个学科分支，少用）

senses.title: The science of earthquakes
senses.definition: the branch of science that studies earthquakes, their causes and their effects
senses.definitionCN: 研究地震、其成因与影响的科学分支
senses.example: She chose seismology because she wanted to understand what happens miles below the surface.
senses.exampleCN: 她选择地震学，是因为想弄清楚地表以下数英里处发生了什么。
senses.why: seismology joins Greek seismos, earthquake, to -logia, the study of something, so the word says exactly what the discipline does.
senses.whyCN: seismology 把希腊 seismos「地震」与 -logia「对某物的研究」拼合，词面正好说出这门学科做什么。

senses.title: The study of seismic waves
senses.definition: the part of the field that reads the waves travelling through rock to infer structure and rupture
senses.definitionCN: 该领域中通过读取岩体中传播的波来推断结构与破裂的部分
senses.example: Modern seismology reads arrivals at hundreds of stations at once.
senses.exampleCN: 现代地震学同时读取数百个台站的到时。
senses.why: earthquakes are known mostly through their waves, so the study of the event became the study of the signal it sends.
senses.whyCN: 地震主要经由其波被认识，因此对事件的研究变成了对它发出的信号的研究。

senses.title: A branch of geophysics
senses.titleCN: 地球物理学的一个分支
senses.definition: the subfield of geophysics that deals with elastic waves and earthquake sources
senses.definitionCN: 地球物理学中处理弹性波与震源问题的子领域
senses.example: Seismology sits beside gravity and magnetism within geophysics.
senses.exampleCN: 在地球物理学中，地震学与重力学、地磁学并列。
senses.why: the discipline defines itself by its physical quantities, and elastic waves are its particular instrument of measurement.
senses.whyCN: 这门学科以所测量的物理量界定自身，而弹性波是它特有的测量手段。

senses.title: Observational network practice
senses.definition: the routine work of operating stations, archiving records and cataloguing events
senses.definitionCN: 运行台站、归档记录与编目事件的日常工作
senses.example: Observational seismology depends on stations that never lose power.
senses.exampleCN: 观测地震学依赖从不掉电的台站。
senses.why: a science built on rare events needs a permanent record, so the adjective observational marks the branch that keeps it.
senses.whyCN: 一门建立在稀有事件上的科学需要永久记录，因此 observational 标出负责保存记录的那一支。

senses.title: Planetary seismology
senses.definition: the application of seismic methods to the Moon, Mars and other solid bodies
senses.definitionCN: 把地震方法用于月球、火星及其他固态天体
senses.example: Planetary seismology detected moonquakes with a single station.
senses.exampleCN: 行星地震学用单个台站探测到了月震。
senses.why: the instrument does not care whether the shaking happens on Earth, so the discipline extended its name to other worlds.
senses.whyCN: 仪器并不在意震动是否发生在地球上，因此这门学科把名字扩展到了别的世界。

senses.title: Exploration seismology
senses.definition: the industrial use of controlled seismic sources to image rock for resources or engineering
senses.definitionCN: 用可控震源为资源或工程目的给岩层成像的工业应用
senses.example: Exploration seismology mapped the reservoir before any well was drilled.
senses.exampleCN: 勘探地震学在任何井开钻之前就勾出了储层。
senses.why: the same theory serves a different goal, so the field is named by its purpose rather than its subject.
senses.whyCN: 同一套理论服务于不同目标，因此这一支按用途而非研究对象命名。

senses.title: Engineering seismology
senses.definition: the branch that estimates ground shaking and supplies design values for structures
senses.definitionCN: 估算地面震动并为结构提供设计参数的分支
senses.example: Engineering seismology turned the fault map into design loads.
senses.exampleCN: 工程地震学把断层图转化为设计荷载。
senses.why: when the question moves from what happened to what to build, the discipline splits off a branch with its own name.
senses.whyCN: 当问题从「发生了什么」转向「该建什么」时，学科便分出一支并另立名目。

senses.title: Historical and computational seismology
senses.titleCN: 历史地震学与计算地震学
senses.definition: the reconstruction of past events from written records, and the numerical modelling of wave propagation
senses.definitionCN: 从文字记录重建过去事件，以及对波传播进行数值模拟
senses.example: Historical seismology pushes the catalogue back three centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 历史地震学把地震目录向前推到三个世纪。
senses.why: both branches work on the same object by other means: one reads old paper, the other runs new code.
senses.whyCN: 两支用不同手段研究同一对象：一支读旧纸，一支跑新代码。

intro.en: Seismology is a modern scientific compound: Greek seismos, earthquake, plus -logia, from logos, word, reason, the study of. It was coined in the nineteenth century and has no Latin ancestor.
intro.cn: seismology 是现代科学复合词：希腊 seismos「地震」加 -logia，后者出自 logos「言说、道理」，意为「对……的研究」。该词于 19 世纪新造，没有拉丁语祖先。

items.en: Seismos meant a shaking or an earthquake, from seiein, to shake. The deeper pre-Greek root is not established and remains reconstructed.
items.cn: seismos 意为震动或地震，来自 seiein「摇动」。其希腊语之前的更深词根未获证明，仍属重构。

items.en: Logos meant word, account or reason; the suffix -logia named the study or account of a subject, as in biology and geology.
items.cn: logos 意为言词、叙述或道理；后缀 -logia 表示对某一主题的研究或叙述，如 biology 与 geology。

items.en: Seismology was formed in English around the 1850s, when earthquake catalogues and instruments made a distinct science possible.
items.cn: seismology 约在 1850 年代在英语中构成，当时地震目录与仪器使一门独立科学成为可能。

items.en: The field split into observational, exploration, engineering and planetary branches as instruments spread and computing arrived.
items.cn: 随着仪器普及与计算技术到来，该领域分成观测、勘探、工程与行星几支。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper root): the earliest printed use is dated only approximately to the 1850s, and the pre-Greek origin of seiein is unsettled.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词根）：最早的印刷用例只能约略定在 1850 年代，seiein 的希腊语之前来源亦无定论。

note.en: Group one holds the instrument-and-person words that cluster around the same stem; group two holds neighbouring earth sciences.
note.cn: 第一组是围绕同一词干的仪器与人名词；第二组是相邻的地球科学学科。

entries.definition: The adjective for anything belonging to seismology, as in a seismological survey or observatory.
entries.definitionCN: 属于地震学的一切事物所用的形容词，如地震学测量或地震观测台。

entries.definition: A person who practises seismology; the -ist suffix marks the practitioner.
entries.definitionCN: 从事地震学的人；-ist 后缀标示从业者。

entries.definition: The measured earthquake activity of a region, not the discipline; it is what seismology studies.
entries.definitionCN: 某地区被测得的地震活动，而非学科本身；它是地震学的研究对象。

entries.definition: The practical method of using elastic waves, especially in exploration; the plural form names a technique, not a science.
entries.definitionCN: 使用弹性波的实用方法，尤用于勘探；复数形式指技术而非学科。

entries.definition: The physics of the whole earth, including gravity, heat and magnetism; seismology is one of its branches.
entries.definitionCN: 研究整个地球物理性质的学科，包括重力、热与磁场；地震学是其分支之一。

entries.definition: The study of rocks, strata and earth history; it overlaps with seismology but does not centre on shaking.
entries.definitionCN: 研究岩石、地层与地球历史；与地震学有交集，但不以震动为核心。

entries.definition: The study of volcanoes and volcanic activity, often paired with seismology because magma movement causes tremors.
entries.definitionCN: 研究火山与火山活动，常与地震学配对，因为岩浆运移会引发震动。

entries.definition: The measurement of the earth's shape and the movement of its surface, used alongside seismic data to track deformation.
entries.definitionCN: 测量地球形状与地表运动，常与地震数据配合追踪形变。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: seismo-, earthquake, plus -logy, study of: the study of earthquakes.
normal.cn: seismo-「地震」加 -logy「研究」：研究地震的学问。

normal.en: The family runs seismology, seismologist, seismological, seismically, seismicity.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 seismology、seismologist、seismological、seismically、seismicity。

normal.en: Instruments mark the field: seismograph, seismometer, seismogram all begin with seismo-.
normal.cn: 仪器标记这门学科：seismograph、seismometer、seismogram 都以 seismo- 开头。

normal.en: Fixed branches: observational, exploration, engineering and planetary seismology.
normal.cn: 固定分支：观测地震学、勘探地震学、工程地震学、行星地震学。

normal.en: -logy words name disciplines, so seismology is the discipline, not an instrument or a person.
normal.cn: -logy 结尾的词命名学科，因此 seismology 是学科，不是仪器或人。

abstract.en: Picture a doctor listening through the ground instead of through a chest.
abstract.cn: 想象一位医生不是听诊胸腔，而是隔着大地听诊。

abstract.en: Picture a library that shelves not books but wobbling lines of ink.
abstract.cn: 想象一座图书馆，架上放的不是书，而是抖动的墨线。

abstract.en: Picture a language in which the only sentence is a wave arriving at a certain hour.
abstract.cn: 想象一种语言，其中唯一的句子就是某时到达的一道波。

examples.en: Seismology advanced quickly once stations could share timing signals.
examples.cn: 台站能共享授时信号之后，地震学迅速进步。

examples.en: Her textbook on seismology is used in both geology and physics departments.
examples.cn: 她的地震学教材同时被地质系与物理系采用。

examples.en: Planetary seismology may yet reveal a liquid core inside Mars.
examples.cn: 行星地震学也许终将揭示火星内部的液态核。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「seismo（地震）+ logy（学科）」——研究地震的学问 → 地震学

root: 希腊 seismos「地震」+ -logia（出自 logos「言说、道理」）→ seismologia 式复合；英语 seismology。希腊来源，无拉丁同族，拉丁词条留空。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses trace one discipline outward: the science of earthquakes, its waves, its parent field, its network work, and then its planetary, industrial, engineering, historical and computational branches.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项由一门学科向外展开：地震的科学、它的波、它的母学科、它的台网工作，再到行星、工业、工程、历史与计算各分支。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a paper drum turning slowly, drawing every tremor as a line.
core.cn: 核心意象：纸鼓缓慢转动，把每一次微震画成一条线。

branches.en: THE SCIENCE: the name points at the discipline as a whole.
branches.cn: 学科整体：名称首先指向这门学问全体。

branches.en: THE METHOD: waves are the instrument, geophysics the frame.
branches.cn: 方法：波是工具，地球物理学是框架。

branches.en: THE RECORD: permanent stations turn rare events into data.
branches.cn: 记录：永久台站把稀有事件变成数据。

branches.en: OTHER BODIES AND OTHER GOALS: the same method leaves Earth or leaves pure research.
branches.cn: 别的天体与别的目标：同一方法离开地球，或离开纯研究。

branches.en: SERVICE AND RECONSTRUCTION: it supplies design loads and rebuilds the past.
branches.cn: 服务与重建：它提供设计荷载，也重建过去。

intro.en: Seismology is a transparent Greek compound: an earthquake stem at the front and a study suffix at the back.
intro.cn: seismology 是一个透明的希腊复合词：前部是「地震」词干，后部是「研究」后缀。

latinIntro.en: Nothing here is Latin: both halves are Greek, and Latin only enters later as the language of scientific publication.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁成分：前后两半都是希腊语，拉丁语只是后来作为科学出版语言进入。

items.example: Seismo- opens both science and instrument names.
items.exampleCN: seismo- 既开启学科名，也开启仪器名。

items.example: The stem is borrowed whole from Greek.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干整体借自希腊语。

items.example: Seismology is taught in the earth sciences building.
items.exampleCN: 地震学在地球科学楼里授课。

items.example: The seismologist read the record at a glance.
items.exampleCN: 地震学家一眼就读懂了记录。

items.example: The seismogram is stored digitally now.
items.exampleCN: 地震记录图如今以数字方式保存。

items.example: The seismograph was invented in the nineteenth century.
items.exampleCN: 地震仪发明于 19 世纪。

items.meaning: an instrument that measures ground motion
items.example: A broadband seismometer detects distant quakes.
items.exampleCN: 宽频地震计能探测远处的地震。

definition_zh: 抓住；夺取；查获；把握
definition_en: to take hold of something suddenly, to take power by force, to find and take illegal goods, or to take an opportunity quickly
core_image: 球擦着指尖飞过，一只手在半空中猛地收拢
scene: 球飞过来的那一瞬，他猛地伸手把球抓住。He seized the ball with both hands.
sceneCN: 这里 seize 是「抓住」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他用双手抓住了球。

senses.title: Take hold suddenly
senses.definition: to take hold of something quickly and firmly
senses.definitionCN: 迅速而牢牢地抓住某物
senses.example: He seized the rope and pulled.
senses.exampleCN: 他抓住绳子用力拉。
senses.why: The basic sense is a sudden grab.
senses.whyCN: 基本义就是突然抓取。

senses.title: Take power
senses.definition: to take control of something by force
senses.definitionCN: 用武力取得对某物的控制
senses.example: The army seized the capital.
senses.exampleCN: 军队夺取了首都。
senses.why: Grabbing extends to political control.
senses.whyCN: 抓取的动作延伸到政治控制。

senses.title: Confiscate
senses.definition: to find and take illegal or forbidden goods
senses.definitionCN: 查获并拿走非法或违禁物品
senses.example: Customs seized the smuggled goods.
senses.exampleCN: 海关查获了走私货物。
senses.why: Officials seize what is not allowed.
senses.whyCN: 官员扣押不允许的物品。

senses.title: Take an opportunity
senses.definition: to take an opportunity quickly before it passes
senses.definitionCN: 趁机会尚未溜走而迅速抓住
senses.example: She seized the chance to study abroad.
senses.exampleCN: 她抓住机会出国留学。
senses.why: An opportunity is grabbed like an object.
senses.whyCN: 机会像实物一样被一把抓住。

intro.en: Seize comes from Old French seisir, to take possession, of Germanic origin.
intro.cn: seize 源自古法语 seisir（占有），其根源为日耳曼语。

items.en: Seisir meant to put in possession.

abstract.en: The last year in school is also the first step out.
abstract.cn: 学校的最后一年，也是走出去的第一步。

examples.en: She is senior to everyone else in the office.
examples.cn: 她比办公室里的其他人都年长。

examples.en: He holds a senior position in the company.
examples.cn: 他在公司担任高级职位。

examples.en: The seniors are planning their graduation.
examples.cn: 毕业班学生正在筹划毕业典礼。

dict_mnemonic.text: senior 是拉丁语 senex（老人）的比较级，本义「更年长的」，后引申为级别更高者与毕业班学生。

root: 源自拉丁语 senex（老人）的比较级 senior，核心义「更年长、地位更高」。

sensesIntro.en: Senior means older, higher in rank, an elder, or a final-year student.
sensesIntro.cn: senior 意为年长的、高级的、前辈或毕业班学生。

core.en: Ahead in years or in rank.
core.cn: 在年岁或级别上更靠前。

branches.en: The older of two people.
branches.cn: 两人中年长的一位。

branches.en: A higher place in a hierarchy.
branches.cn: 等级体系中更高的位置。

branches.en: A person who has gone before.
branches.cn: 先走过一段路的人。

branches.en: The oldest class in a school.
branches.cn: 学校里年级最高的班级。

branches.en: Age and rank share one comparison.
branches.cn: 年龄与级别共用一个比较形式。

intro.en: Senior belongs to the Latin senex family of age and rank.
intro.cn: senior 属于拉丁语 senex（老）词族，关联年龄与级别。

latinIntro.en: Latin senex and its comparative senior are the historical base.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 senex 及其比较级 senior 是历史词根。

items.example: The seniors welcomed the new staff.
The senator gave a short speech.
